correctness.rationale: The complete spectral decomposition gives the two exact off-diagonal weights; exact sign fourth moments give the finite profile energy. A strict exchange eliminates all but A0/A1 among split-clique profiles; A1 is uniformly dominated for q>=4. Convex balancing and strictly increasing differences classify joined profiles; E_A0-E_B0=beta*floor(q^2/4)-1 gives all strict/equality regimes. Exact tests from the embedded Python script passed 9808 profile comparisons, 760 independent inverse/variance checks and 47 exact critical identities. Finite tests are not substituted for the analytic all-q proof.

value.rationale: For every q>=4 the theorem proves the exact screening threshold at which an ordinary proper three-coloring becomes globally inferior to deliberately placing adjacent hubs in the same probe class, at unchanged three-query budget. It also classifies every resulting nonproper optimum by a strictly discrete-convex formula with at most two neighboring optimal counts, supplying a natural complete benchmark for the first two-hub split graph family. This is more than recomputing the fixed-partition variance or a single ad hoc finite example; limitations on practical speedups and other sampling laws are explicit.
